title: Power Apps: header and navigation refresh for model-driven apps
summary: The briefing passes: its rollout facts, licensing requirement and maker control are supported by the roadmap and Microsoft Learn. The maker navigation path needs only a minor clarification to include choosing the environment.

claims.claim: Learn says the mail app supports the modern, refreshed look and describes its enablement.
claims.quote: The mail app supports the modern, refreshed look. It's on by default for environments on the monthly channel as part of the February 2026 release, and will be enabled on the semi-annual channel with the October 2026 update.

claims.claim: The maker path is Solutions > solution > Apps > app > Edit > Settings > Features > Header and navigation refresh.
claims.quote: In the app designer, select Settings on the command bar. Select Features, and then enable Header and navigation refresh.
claims.fix: Include environment selection: 'environment > Solutions > solution > Apps > app > Edit > Settings > Features > Header and navigation refresh'. The cited create-edit-app page's 'Edit an app' section says to choose the environment before selecting Solutions; its remaining entry steps and the feature page's final steps match the printed path.

claims.claim: The maker must save and publish the app after changing its settings.
claims.quote: You must select Publish to activate an app settings change. ... Save and Publish the app.

claims.claim: No API call identifying the header and navigation refresh setting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "header and navigation refresh" SaveSettingValue; "header and navigation refresh" API setting definition. Opened modern-fluent-design, savesettingvalue, get-update-setting-value-using-code and create-edit-configure-settings; none identifies the refresh's SettingName.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; controls[0].scope; Governance controls; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The maker setting controls whether the refresh is enabled for an individual existing app.
claims.quote: Enable the header and navigation refresh for an existing app ... In the app designer, select Settings on the command bar. Select Features, and then enable Header and navigation refresh.

claims.claim: An environment-wide switch for this specific refresh is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "header and navigation refresh" "tenant" "environment" switch; "header and navigation refresh" "setting" "unique". Read modern-fluent-design and create-edit-configure-settings; no refresh setting definition or its allowed environment override scope is identified.

claims.claim: A tenant-wide switch for the header and navigation refresh itself is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "header and navigation refresh" "tenant" "environment" switch. Read modern-fluent-design, app-properties and create-edit-configure-settings; no tenant-wide refresh switch is documented.

claims.claim: The generic SaveSettingValue action creates or updates an app or organization level setting override.
claims.quote: Creates or updates app/organization level override.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not state the unique name of the header and navigation refresh setting.
claims.quote: Searched: "header and navigation refresh" "setting" "unique"; "header and navigation refresh" "SettingName" API environment admin. Read modern-fluent-design, savesettingvalue, client API settings reference and create-edit-configure-settings; no unique name found.

claims.claim: The generic action is not documented with a setting identifier establishing a call for this refresh.
claims.quote: Searched: "header and navigation refresh" SaveSettingValue; "header and navigation refresh" API setting definition. SaveSettingValue requires a setting definition unique name; the feature page and generic settings references do not provide that mapping for the refresh.

claims.claim: Learn documents a separate New look for model driven apps setting that can be added to a solution.
claims.quote: Select Add Existing > More > Setting. ... Select New look for model driven apps. Select Add to add it to the solution.

claims.claim: The Learn feature page still contains revert instructions saying admins can turn off the New Look.
claims.quote: Admins can turn off the New Look for all users by updating the New look for model driven apps app setting.

claims.claim: Learn also says the New Look is mandatory, unlike the opt-in header and navigation refresh.
claims.quote: By the April 2026 semiannual release, all users must use the New Look (wave 1 of the modernization arc). ... This requirement doesn't include the header and navigation refresh (wave 2).

claims.claim: The app settings page says the New Look setting is hidden and ignored with the 2026 Wave 1 release.
claims.quote: This setting is hidden and ignored with the 2026 Wave 1 release when the new look becomes mandatory.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a mandatory-adoption date for the header and navigation refresh.
claims.quote: Searched: "header and navigation refresh" "mandatory"; "header and navigation refresh" mandatory deadline permissions security data movement autonomous. Read modern-fluent-design: wave 2 is opt-in and explicitly excluded from the wave 1 mandate.

claims.claim: Enabling the setting changes the app experience for its users rather than only the maker's personal view.
claims.quote: When you select Settings from the command bar, select Features to enable or disable model-driven app features for the app.
